Color temperature.subject: Applied Sciences
Color temperature.question: The _____ was Property of light sources related to black-body radiation.
Color temperature.fact: Color temperature is a parameter describing the color of a visible light source by comparing it to the color of light emitted by an idealized opaque, non-reflective body. The temperature of the ideal emitter that matches the color most closely is defined as the color temperature of the original visible light source.

Color temperature.subject: Applied Sciences
Color temperature.question: Rayleigh scattering of sunlight by _____'s atmosphere causes the blue color of the sky, which tends to scatter blue light more than red light
Color temperature.fact: The effective temperature, defined by the total radiative power per square unit, is 5,772 K. The color temperature of sunlight above the atmosphere is about 5,900 K. The Sun may appear red, orange, yellow, or white from Earth, depending on its position in the sky. Rayleigh scattering of sunlight by Earth's atmosphere causes the blue color of the sky, which tends to scatter blue light more than red light.

Combination.question: The _____ was Selection of items from a set.
Combination.fact: In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations). For example, given three fruits, say an apple, an orange and a pear, there are three combinations of two that can be drawn from this set: an apple and a pear; an apple and an orange; or a pear and an orange.

Completeness (order theory).fact: In the mathematical area of order theory, completeness properties assert the existence of certain infima or suprema of a given partially ordered set (poset). The most familiar example is the completeness of the real numbers.

Completeness (order theory).subject: Applied Sciences
Completeness (order theory).question: Details on this characterization can be found in the articles on the "lattice-like" structures for which this is typically considered: see semilattice, lattice, _____ algebra, and Boolean algebra
Completeness (order theory).fact: Details on this characterization can be found in the articles on the "lattice-like" structures for which this is typically considered: see semilattice, lattice, Heyting algebra, and Boolean algebra.

Completeness (order theory).subject: Applied Sciences
Completeness (order theory).question: In fact this approach offers additional insights both into the nature of many completeness properties and into the importance of _____ connections for order theory
Completeness (order theory).fact: In fact this approach offers additional insights both into the nature of many completeness properties and into the importance of Galois connections for order theory. The general observation on which this reformulation of completeness is based is that the construction of certain suprema or infima provides left or right adjoint parts of suitable Galois connections.

Completeness (order theory).question: The general observation on which this reformulation of completeness is based is that the construction of certain suprema or infima provides left or right adjoint parts of suitable _____ connections
Completeness (order theory).fact: In fact this approach offers additional insights both into the nature of many completeness properties and into the importance of Galois connections for order theory. The general observation on which this reformulation of completeness is based is that the construction of certain suprema or infima provides left or right adjoint parts of suitable Galois connections.

Completeness (order theory).subject: Applied Sciences
Completeness (order theory).question: As a first simple example, let _____ = {*} be a specified one-element set with the only possible partial ordering
Completeness (order theory).fact: As a first simple example, let 1 = {*} be a specified one-element set with the only possible partial ordering. There is an obvious mapping j: X → 1 with j(x) = * for all x in X. X has a least element if and only if the function j has a lower adjoint j*: 1 → X. Indeed the definition for Galois connections yields that in this case j*(*) ≤ x if and only if * ≤ j(x), where the right hand side obviously holds for any x.

Complex analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex analysis.question: The _____ was Branch of mathematics studying functions of a complex variable.
Complex analysis.fact: Complex analysis, traditionally called the theory of functions of a complex variable, is the branch of mathematical analysis that studies complex-valued functions of one or more complex variables. Complex analysis primarily studies holomorphic functions, which are differentiable functions of a complex variable.

Complex analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex analysis.question: Important mathematicians associated with complex numbers include Euler, Gauss, _____, Cauchy, Weierstrass, and many more in the 20th century
Complex analysis.fact: Important mathematicians associated with complex numbers include Euler, Gauss, Riemann, Cauchy, Weierstrass, and many more in the 20th century.

Complex analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex analysis.question: In particular, if a complex function has a derivative, it has derivatives of every order and equals the sum of its _____ series in a neighborhood of every point of its domain
Complex analysis.fact: In particular, if a complex function has a derivative, it has derivatives of every order and equals the sum of its Taylor series in a neighborhood of every point of its domain.

Complex analysis.question: {\displaystyle f'(z_{0})=\lim _{z\to z_{0}}{\frac {f(z)-f(z_{0})}{z-z_{0}}}.} _____, this definition is formally analogous to that of the derivative of a real function
Complex analysis.fact: {\displaystyle f'(z_{0})=\lim _{z\to z_{0}}{\frac {f(z)-f(z_{0})}{z-z_{0}}}.} Superficially, this definition is formally analogous to that of the derivative of a real function.

Complex analysis.fact: In essence, this means that functions holomorphic on Ω {\displaystyle \Omega } can be approximated arbitrarily well by polynomials in some neighborhood of every point in Ω {\displaystyle \Omega }.

Complex analysis.question: The line integral around a closed path of a function that is holomorphic everywhere inside the area bounded by the closed path is always zero, as is stated by the _____ integral theorem
Complex analysis.fact: The line integral around a closed path of a function that is holomorphic everywhere inside the area bounded by the closed path is always zero, as is stated by the Cauchy integral theorem. The values of such a holomorphic function inside a disk can be computed by a path integral on the disk's boundary (as shown in Cauchy's integral formula).

Complex analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex analysis.question: The values of such a holomorphic function inside a disk can be computed by a path integral on the disk's boundary (as shown in _____'s integral formula)
Complex analysis.fact: The line integral around a closed path of a function that is holomorphic everywhere inside the area bounded by the closed path is always zero, as is stated by the Cauchy integral theorem. Complex analysis.question: The remarkable behavior of holomorphic functions near essential singularities is described by _____'s theorem
Complex analysis.fact: The remarkable behavior of holomorphic functions near essential singularities is described by Picard's theorem.

Complex analysis.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex analysis.question: A bounded function that is holomorphic in the entire complex plane must be constant; this is _____'s theorem
Complex analysis.fact: A bounded function that is holomorphic in the entire complex plane must be constant; this is Liouville's theorem.

Complex conjugate.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex conjugate.question: The _____ was Fundamental operation on complex numbers.
Complex conjugate.fact: In mathematics, the complex conjugate of a complex number is the number with an equal real part and an imaginary part equal in magnitude but opposite in sign. Complex coordinate space.question: The _____ was Space formed by the ''n''-tuples of complex numbers.
Complex coordinate space.fact: In mathematics, the n-dimensional complex coordinate space (or complex n-space) is the set of all ordered n-tuples of complex numbers, also called complex vectors.

Complex coordinate space.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex coordinate space.question: The space is denoted C n {\displaystyle \mathbb {C} ^{n}} , and is the n-fold _____ product of the complex line C {\displaystyle \mathbb {C} } with itself
Complex coordinate space.fact: The space is denoted C n {\displaystyle \mathbb {C} ^{n}} , and is the n-fold Cartesian product of the complex line C {\displaystyle \mathbb {C} } with itself.

Complex coordinate space.question: With the standard _____ topology, C n {\displaystyle \mathbb {C} ^{n}} is a topological vector space over the complex numbers
Complex coordinate space.fact: With the standard Euclidean topology, C n {\displaystyle \mathbb {C} ^{n}} is a topological vector space over the complex numbers.

Complex plane.subject: Applied Sciences
Complex plane.question: The _____ was Geometric representation of the complex numbers.
Complex plane.fact: In mathematics, the complex plane is the plane formed by the complex numbers, with a Cartesian coordinate system such that the horizontal x-axis, called the real axis, is formed by the real numbers, and the vertical y-axis, called the imaginary axis, is formed by the imaginary numbers. Composite number.subject: Applied Sciences

Composite number.fact: A composite number is a positive integer that can be formed by multiplying two smaller positive integers. Every positive integer is composite, prime, or the unit 1, so the composite numbers are exactly the natural numbers that are not prime and not a unit.

Flight planning.fact: AIRAC (Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control) occurs every fourth Thursday, when every country publishes its changes, which are usually to airways.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: For example, Amsterdam Schiphol Airport has an elevation of −_____
Flight planning.fact: For example, Amsterdam Schiphol Airport has an elevation of −3 metres.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: The surface of the Dead Sea is _____ below sea level, so low-level flights in this vicinity can be well below sea level
Flight planning.fact: The surface of the Dead Sea is 417 metres below sea level, so low-level flights in this vicinity can be well below sea level.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Since 1979, the _____ (ICAO) has recommended a unification of units of measurement within aviation based on the International System of Units (SI)
Flight planning.fact: Since 1979, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) has recommended a unification of units of measurement within aviation based on the International System of Units (SI).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: In a flight plan, a Mach number of "Point 82" means that the aircraft is travelling at 0.820 (_____) of the speed of sound
Flight planning.fact: In a flight plan, a Mach number of "Point 82" means that the aircraft is travelling at 0.820 (82%) of the speed of sound.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Within these airways, aircraft must maintain flight levels, specified altitudes usually separated vertically by 1,000 or _____ (300 or 610 m), depending on the route being flown and the direction of t
Flight planning.fact: Within these airways, aircraft must maintain flight levels, specified altitudes usually separated vertically by 1,000 or 2,000 ft (300 or 610 m), depending on the route being flown and the direction of travel.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Major airports may have runways that are about _____ (3 km) long, so merely taxiing from the terminal to the end of the runway might consume up to a ton of fuel
Flight planning.fact: Major airports may have runways that are about 2 miles (3 km) long, so merely taxiing from the terminal to the end of the runway might consume up to a ton of fuel.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Since 2010, ICAO recommends using: _____ per hour (km/h) for speed during travel
Flight planning.fact: Since 2010, ICAO recommends using: Kilometers per hour (km/h) for speed during travel. Kilometers (km) for distance.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: In most areas, height is reported as a multiple of _____ (30 m), i.e
Flight planning.fact: In most areas, height is reported as a multiple of 100 feet (30 m), i.e.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: These are expressed as a three-figure group e.g., FL320 is _____ (9,800 m) ISA
Flight planning.fact: These are expressed as a three-figure group e.g., FL320 is 32,000 ft (9,800 m) ISA.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: In most areas, the vertical separation between aircraft is either 1,000 or _____ (300 or 610 m)
Flight planning.fact: These are expressed as a three-figure group e.g., FL320 is 32,000 ft (9,800 m) ISA. In most areas, the vertical separation between aircraft is either 1,000 or 2,000 ft (300 or 610 m).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: The vertical separation between aircraft is either _____ or 600 metres (about 1.6% less than 1,000 or 2,000 feet)
Flight planning.fact: The vertical separation between aircraft is either 300 metres or 600 metres (about 1.6% less than 1,000 or 2,000 feet).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Until 1999, the vertical separation between aircraft flying at high altitudes on the same airway was _____ (610 m)
Flight planning.fact: The vertical separation between aircraft is either 300 metres or 600 metres (about 1.6% less than 1,000 or 2,000 feet). Until 1999, the vertical separation between aircraft flying at high altitudes on the same airway was 2,000 feet (610 m).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: This cuts the vertical separation to _____ (300 m) between flight levels 290 and 410 (the exact limits vary slightly from place to place)
Flight planning.fact: This cuts the vertical separation to 1,000 feet (300 m) between flight levels 290 and 410 (the exact limits vary slightly from place to place).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: This "ton" is generally either a metric tonne or a UK long ton, which differ by less than _____, or a short ton, which is about 10% less
Flight planning.fact: This "ton" is generally either a metric tonne or a UK long ton, which differ by less than 2%, or a short ton, which is about 10% less.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Waypoints use five letters (e.g., _____), and those that double as non-directional beacons use three or two (TNN, WK)
Flight planning.fact: Waypoints use five letters (e.g., PILOX), and those that double as non-directional beacons use three or two (TNN, WK).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: A geographic waypoint is a temporary position used in a flight plan, usually in an area where there are no named waypoints (e.g., most oceans in the _____)
Flight planning.fact: A geographic waypoint is a temporary position used in a flight plan, usually in an area where there are no named waypoints (e.g., most oceans in the Southern Hemisphere).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Much of the descent portion of a flight will take place on a _____
Flight planning.fact: Before landing, an aircraft follows an arrival procedure (standard terminal arrival route, or STAR), which defines a pathway from a waypoint on an airway to an airport runway, so that the aircraft can leave the airway system in a controlled manner. Much of the descent portion of a flight will take place on a STAR.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Special routes known as ocean tracks are used across some oceans, mainly in the _____, to increase traffic capacity on busy routes
Flight planning.fact: Special routes called ocean tracks are used across some oceans, mainly in the Northern Hemisphere, to increase traffic capacity on busy routes.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Ocean tracks may start and finish about _____ offshore at named waypoints, to which a number of airways connect
Flight planning.fact: Ocean tracks may start and finish about 100 miles offshore at named waypoints, to which a number of airways connect.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: This calculation is somewhat complicated: _____ of fuel burn depends on ambient temperature, aircraft speed, and aircraft altitude, none of which are entirely predictable
Flight planning.fact: This calculation is somewhat complicated: Rate of fuel burn depends on ambient temperature, aircraft speed, and aircraft altitude, none of which are entirely predictable. Rate of fuel burn also depends on airplane weight, which changes as fuel is burned.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Each 6-hour forecast covers the whole world using grid points located at intervals of 75 nautical miles (_____) or less
Flight planning.fact: Each 6-hour forecast covers the whole world using grid points located at intervals of 75 nautical miles (139 km) or less. For 75-nautical-mile (139 km) intervals, linear interpolation is satisfactory.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: For 75-nautical-mile (_____) intervals, linear interpolation is satisfactory
Flight planning.fact: Each 6-hour forecast covers the whole world using grid points located at intervals of 75 nautical miles (139 km) or less. For 75-nautical-mile (139 km) intervals, linear interpolation is satisfactory.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: At each grid point, the wind speed, wind direction, air temperature is supplied at nine different heights between 4,500 and _____ (1,400 and 16,800 m)
Flight planning.fact: At each grid point, the wind speed, wind direction, air temperature is supplied at nine different heights between 4,500 and 55,000 feet (1,400 and 16,800 m).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: The GRIB format superseded the earlier ADF format in _____–99
Flight planning.fact: The GRIB format superseded the earlier ADF format in 1998–99.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Physical constraints _____ all the weights mentioned above in "Overview and basic terminology" may be subject to minimum and/or maximum values
Flight planning.fact: Physical constraints Almost all the weights mentioned above in "Overview and basic terminology" may be subject to minimum and/or maximum values.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Many situations have tens or even hundreds of possible routes, and there are some situations with over 25,000 possible routes (e.g., London to _____ with free-flight below the track system)
Flight planning.fact: Many situations have tens or even hundreds of possible routes, and there are some situations with over 25,000 possible routes (e.g., London to New York with free-flight below the track system).

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Note that discontinuities due to changes in flight levels can mean that a difference of as little as _____ (one passenger with luggage) in zero fuel weight or tankering fuel can make the difference be
Flight planning.fact: Note that discontinuities due to changes in flight levels can mean that a difference of as little as 100 kg (one passenger with luggage) in zero fuel weight or tankering fuel can make the difference between profit and loss.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Inflight diversion _____ en route, an aircraft may be diverted to some airport other than the planned alternate
Flight planning.fact: Inflight diversion While en route, an aircraft may be diverted to some airport other than the planned alternate.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: Inflight refuelling _____ aircraft may refuel in midair
Flight planning.fact: Inflight refuelling Military aircraft may refuel in midair.

Flight planning.subject: Applied Sciences
Flight planning.question: The _____ format superseded the earlier ADF format in 1998–99
Flight planning.fact: The GRIB format superseded the earlier ADF format in 1998–99. The ADF format used 300-nautical-mile (560 km) intervals; this interval was large enough to miss some storms completely, so calculations using ADF-predicted weather were often not as accurate as those that can be produced using GRIB-predicted weather.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: The _____ was Exhaust for a fireplace, furnace etc.
Flue.fact: A flue is a pipe, or opening in a chimney for conveying exhaust gases from a fireplace, furnace, water heater, boiler, or generator to the outdoors. Historically the term flue meant the chimney itself.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: In the _____, they are also known as vents for boilers and as breeching for water heaters and modern furnaces
Flue.fact: In the United States, they are also called vents for boilers and as breeching for water heaters and modern furnaces.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: Vent connectors join the appliance outlet to the vent or chimney; they are part of the venting system and are distinct from _____ ductwork
Flue.fact: Vent connectors join the appliance outlet to the vent or chimney; they are part of the venting system and are distinct from HVAC ductwork.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: The fuel gas code provides prescriptive sizing for natural-draft venting systems serving one or more listed appliances (including draft-hood and fan-assisted _____ I units listed for Type B vent)
Flue.fact: The fuel gas code provides prescriptive sizing for natural-draft venting systems serving one or more listed appliances (including draft-hood and fan-assisted Category I units listed for Type B vent).

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: Mixing components from different vent manufacturers is not permitted in UL-_____ systems
Flue.fact: Where plastic piping is used, the appliance must be listed for that venting material; plastic vent systems either follow the appliance-specified product standards or are listed and labeled to UL 1738 (USA) and installed per the vent manufacturer’s instructions (including requirements such as contrasting-color primer where applicable). Mixing components from different vent manufacturers is not permitted in UL-1738 systems.

Flue.subject: Applied Sciences
Flue.question: Observe maximum horizontal lengths and required clearances to combustibles per code and listing (e.g., single-wall connector max length typically _____ of chimney/vent height, unless engineered)
Flue.fact: Observe maximum horizontal lengths and required clearances to combustibles per code and listing (e.g., single-wall connector max length typically 75% of chimney/vent height, unless engineered).

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: The _____ was Branch of physics.
Fluid mechanics.fact: Fluid mechanics is the branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids (liquids, gases, and plasmas) and the forces on them.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: Occasionally, body forces, such as the gravitational force or _____ force are added to the equations
Fluid mechanics.fact: Occasionally, body forces, such as the gravitational force or Lorentz force are added to the equations.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: These cases generally involve non-turbulent, steady flow in which the _____ number is small
Fluid mechanics.fact: These cases generally involve non-turbulent, steady flow in which the Reynolds number is small.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: For fluid flow over a porous boundary, the fluid velocity can be discontinuous between the free fluid and the fluid in the porous media (this is related to the _____ and Joseph condition)
Fluid mechanics.fact: For fluid flow over a porous boundary, the fluid velocity can be discontinuous between the free fluid and the fluid in the porous media (this is related to the Beavers and Joseph condition).

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: For example, water is a _____ fluid, because it continues to display fluid properties no matter how much it is stirred or mixed
Fluid mechanics.fact: For example, water is a Newtonian fluid, because it continues to display fluid properties no matter how much it is stirred or mixed. Important fluids, like water as well as most gasses, behave—to good approximation—as a Newtonian fluid under normal conditions on Earth.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: Important fluids, like water as well as most gasses, behave—to good approximation—as a _____ fluid under normal conditions on Earth
Fluid mechanics.fact: For example, water is a Newtonian fluid, because it continues to display fluid properties no matter how much it is stirred or mixed. Important fluids, like water as well as most gasses, behave—to good approximation—as a Newtonian fluid under normal conditions on Earth.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: By contrast, stirring a non-_____ fluid can leave a "hole" behind
Fluid mechanics.fact: For example, water is a Newtonian fluid, because it continues to display fluid properties no matter how much it is stirred or mixed. Important fluids, like water as well as most gasses, behave—to good approximation—as a Newtonian fluid under normal conditions on Earth.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: Alternatively, stirring a non-_____ fluid can cause the viscosity to decrease, so the fluid appears "thinner" (this is seen in non-drip paints)
Fluid mechanics.fact: Important fluids, like water as well as most gasses, behave—to good approximation—as a Newtonian fluid under normal conditions on Earth. By contrast, stirring a non-Newtonian fluid can leave a "hole" behind.

Fluid mechanics.subject: Applied Sciences
Fluid mechanics.question: The equation reduced in this form is called the _____ equation
Fluid mechanics.fact: The equation reduced in this form is called the Euler equation.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: The _____ was Sequence of words formed by specific rules.
Formal language.fact: In logic, mathematics, computer science, and linguistics, a formal language is a set of strings whose symbols are taken from a set called "alphabet". The alphabet of a formal language consists of symbols that concatenate into strings (also called "words").

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: Later, _____ investigated the problem of Gauss codes
Formal language.fact: Later, Carl Friedrich Gauss investigated the problem of Gauss codes.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: In the mid-19th century, _____ established the field of boolean algebra, which is a formal way of describing logical operations using truth values and set operators
Formal language.fact: In the mid-19th century, George Boole set up the field of boolean algebra, which is a formal way of describing logical operations using truth values and set operators.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: In his work _____ of The Laws of Thought, he demonstrated that logical reasoning can be expressed and manipulated through symbolic equations
Formal language.fact: In his work An Investigation of The Laws of Thought, he demonstrated that logical reasoning can be expressed and manipulated through symbolic equations.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: Gottlob Frege attempted to realize Leibniz's ideas, through a notational system, first outlined in Begriffsschrift (_____) and more fully developed in his 2-volume Grundgesetze der Arithmetik (1893/19
Formal language.fact: Gottlob Frege attempted to realize Leibniz's ideas, through a notational system, first outlined in Begriffsschrift (1879) and more fully developed in his 2-volume Grundgesetze der Arithmetik (1893/1903).

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: Axel Thue published four papers relating to words and language between _____ and 1914
Formal language.fact: Axel Thue published four papers relating to words and language between 1906 and 1914.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: The last of these introduced what _____ later termed 'Thue Systems', and gave an early example of an undecidable problem
Formal language.fact: The last of these introduced what Emil Post later termed 'Thue Systems', and gave an early example of an undecidable problem.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: Post would later use this paper as the basis for a _____ proof "that the word problem for semigroups was recursively insoluble", and later devised the canonical system for the creation of formal langu
Formal language.fact: Post would later use this paper as the basis for a 1947 proof "that the word problem for semigroups was recursively insoluble", and later devised the canonical system for the creation of formal languages.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: In _____, Leonardo Torres Quevedo introduced a formal language for the description of mechanical drawings (mechanical devices), in Vienna
Formal language.fact: In 1907, Leonardo Torres Quevedo introduced a formal language for the description of mechanical drawings (mechanical devices), in Vienna.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: Noam _____ devised an abstract representation of formal and natural languages, known as the Chomsky hierarchy
Formal language.fact: Noam Chomsky devised an abstract representation of formal and natural languages, called the Chomsky hierarchy.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: In _____ John Backus developed the Backus-Naur form to describe the syntax of a high level programming language, following his work in the creation of FORTRAN
Formal language.fact: In 1959 John Backus developed the Backus-Naur form to describe the syntax of a high level programming language, following his work in the creation of FORTRAN.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: Peter Naur was the secretary/editor for the ALGOL60 _____ in which he used Backus–Naur form to describe the Formal part of ALGOL60
Formal language.fact: Peter Naur was the secretary/editor for the ALGOL60 Report in which he used Backus–Naur form to describe the Formal part of ALGOL60.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: It often makes sense to use an alphabet in the usual sense of the word, or more generally any finite character encoding such as ASCII or _____
Formal language.fact: It often makes sense to use an alphabet in the usual sense of the word, or more generally any finite character encoding such as ASCII or Unicode.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: The set of all words over an alphabet Σ is usually denoted by Σ* (using the _____ star)
Formal language.fact: The set of all words over an alphabet Σ is usually denoted by Σ* (using the Kleene star).

Formal language.fact: We call the set Σ {\displaystyle \Sigma } the alphabet of L {\displaystyle L}. On the other hand, given a formal language L {\displaystyle L} over Σ {\displaystyle \Sigma } , a word w ∈ Σ ∗ {\displaystyle w\in \Sigma ^{*}} is well-formed if w ∈ L {\displaystyle w\in L}.

Formal language.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal language.question: This described a "formal language of pure language." In the first half of the _____th century, several developments were made with relevance to formal languages
Formal language.fact: This described a "formal language of pure language." In the first half of the 20th century, several developments were made with relevance to formal languages.

Formal science.subject: Applied Sciences
Formal science.question: The _____ was Study of abstract structures described by formal systems.
Formal science.fact: Formal science is a branch of science studying disciplines concerned with abstract structures described by formal systems. Whereas the natural sciences and social sciences seek to characterize physical systems and social systems, respectively, using theoretical and empirical methods, the formal sciences use language tools concerned with characterizing abstract structures described by formal systems and the deductions that can be made from them.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: The _____ was Basic framework of mathematics.
Foundations of mathematics.fact: Foundations of mathematics are the logical and mathematical frameworks that allow the development of mathematics without generating self-contradictory theories, and to have reliable concepts of theorems, proofs, algorithms, etc. The term "foundations of mathematics" was not coined before the end of the 19th century, although foundations were first set up by the ancient Greek philosophers under the name of Aristotle's logic and systematically applied in Euclid's Elements.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: These foundations were tacitly assumed to be definitive until the introduction of infinitesimal calculus by Isaac Newton and _____ in the 17th century
Foundations of mathematics.fact: These foundations were tacitly assumed to be definitive until the introduction of infinitesimal calculus by Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz in the 17th century.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: This framework is based on a systematic use of axiomatic method and on set theory, specifically _____–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice
Foundations of mathematics.fact: This framework is based on a systematic use of axiomatic method and on set theory, specifically Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the axiom of choice.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: It seems that ancient _____ philosophers were the first to study the nature of mathematics and its relation with the real world
Foundations of mathematics.fact: It seems that ancient Greek philosophers were the first to study the nature of mathematics and its relation with the real world.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: His method anticipated that of Dedekind cuts in the modern definition of real numbers by Richard Dedekind (_____–1916); see Eudoxus of Cnidus § Eudoxus' proportions
Foundations of mathematics.fact: His method anticipated that of Dedekind cuts in the modern definition of real numbers by Richard Dedekind (1831–1916); see Eudoxus of Cnidus § Eudoxus' proportions.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: In the _____, Aristotle (384–322 BC) laid down the logic for organizing a field of knowledge by means of primitive concepts, axioms, postulates, definitions, and theorems
Foundations of mathematics.fact: In the Posterior Analytics, Aristotle (384–322 BC) laid down the logic for organizing a field of knowledge by means of primitive concepts, axioms, postulates, definitions, and theorems.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: So, for _____, a proved theorem is true, while in the axiomatic methods, the proof says only that the axioms imply the statement of the theorem
Foundations of mathematics.fact: In the Posterior Analytics, Aristotle (384–322 BC) laid down the logic for organizing a field of knowledge by means of primitive concepts, axioms, postulates, definitions, and theorems. Aristotle took a majority of his examples for this from arithmetic and from geometry, and his logic served as the foundation of mathematics for centuries.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: In _____, René Descartes published La Géométrie, in which he showed that geometry can be reduced to algebra by means of coordinates, which are numbers determining the position of a point
Foundations of mathematics.fact: In 1637, René Descartes published La Géométrie, in which he showed that geometry can be reduced to algebra by means of coordinates, which are numbers determining the position of a point.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: Descartes' book became famous after _____ and paved the way to infinitesimal calculus
Foundations of mathematics.fact: Descartes' book became famous after 1649 and paved the way to infinitesimal calculus.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: Real numbers, continuous functions, derivatives were not formally defined before the 19th century, as well as _____ geometry
Foundations of mathematics.fact: Real numbers, continuous functions, derivatives were not formally defined before the 19th century, as well as Euclidean geometry.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: In 1637, René _____ published La Géométrie, in which he showed that geometry can be reduced to algebra by means of coordinates, which are numbers determining the position of a point
Foundations of mathematics.fact: In 1637, René Descartes published La Géométrie, in which he showed that geometry can be reduced to algebra by means of coordinates, which are numbers determining the position of a point. Descartes' book became famous after 1649 and paved the way to infinitesimal calculus.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: The modern (ε, δ)-definition of limits and continuous functions was first developed by Bolzano in _____, but remained relatively unknown, and Cauchy probably did know Bolzano's work
Foundations of mathematics.fact: The modern (ε, δ)-definition of limits and continuous functions was first developed by Bolzano in 1817, but remained relatively unknown, and Cauchy probably did know Bolzano's work.

Foundations of mathematics.subject: Applied Sciences
Foundations of mathematics.question: Firstly both definitions suppose that rational numbers and thus natural numbers are rigorously defined; this was done a few years later with _____ axioms
Foundations of mathematics.fact: Firstly both definitions suppose that rational numbers and thus natural numbers are rigorously defined; this was done a few years later with Peano axioms.

Nonetheless, executing the entire sequence once produces the output (3, 5), but executing it a second time produces the output (5, 5), so the sequence is not idempotent.

Metallurgy.fact: With the Carpatho-Balkan region described as the 'earliest metallurgical province in Eurasia', its scale and technical quality of metal production in the 6th~5th millennia BCE totally overshadowed that of any other contemporary production centre.
